customManagers.description: Container image tags hard-coded in Testcontainers Java sources. No built-in manager reads .java files, so postgres:15.3 and ghcr.io/shopify/toxiproxy:2.10.0 would otherwise never be updated. Both alternatives are anchored on a Testcontainers construct so that unrelated colon-bearing literals in these files ("postgres:5432", "0.0.0.0:8666", "jdbc:postgresql://...", CSV timestamps like 17:31:31.00) cannot match. The optional currentDigest group keeps the manager matching after pinDigests rewrites the literal to name:tag@sha256:...

packageRules.description: Exclude OpenRewrite Gradle plugin 7.40.0 and 7.41.0 because their public Plugin Portal publications depend on org.openrewrite BOM artifacts that are available only from the credentialed Code Genome Project. Later versions remain eligible when publicly resolvable.
Bundle every non-major update into one automergeable pull request. Majors are deliberately excluded so a pending major never blocks the automergeable bundle.

Major updates land one at a time and are merged by a human after review of the migration notes. This rule deliberately does not set groupName: majors are already ungrouped because the bundle above matches non-major types only, and forcing groupName here would split lockstep groups whose members must move together across a major boundary.

Lockstep: every org.testcontainers artifact ships from one repository under one version number, and the modules resolve the core at their own version. `gradlew dependencies --configuration testRuntimeClasspath` currently reports `org.testcontainers:junit-jupiter:1.21.4 -> org.testcontainers:testcontainers:1.21.4 -> 2.0.5` for junit-jupiter, postgresql and toxiproxy, i.e. core has already crossed a major alone and Gradle is silently forcing three modules onto an unintended core. A shared groupName makes the next major boundary a single reviewed pull request instead of four.

Lockstep: junit-bom pins the versions that junit-jupiter and junit-platform-launcher resolve to. The build declares platform(org.junit:junit-bom) plus two versionless artifacts, so the BOM major and any artifact major must be the same pull request.

Lockstep: net.jqwik:jqwik depends on net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at its exact version (verified in the resolved testRuntimeClasspath tree), and both are declared separately here (jqwik as testImplementation, jqwik-engine as testRuntimeOnly). Split majors would put jqwik-api and the JUnit platform engine implementation on different versions and the jqwik engine would fail to register.

Lockstep: the org.openrewrite.rewrite Gradle plugin and the recipe artifact on the `rewrite` configuration must agree on rewrite-core. `gradlew buildEnvironment` shows plugin 7.38.0 -> org.openrewrite:plugin:7.38.0 -> org.openrewrite:rewrite-bom:8.88.0, and rewrite-migrate-java:3.41.0 pulls org.openrewrite:rewrite-java:8.88.0. A recipe compiled against a newer rewrite-core than the plugin loads fails at recipe-run time, not at configuration time.

Lockstep: the org.graalvm.buildtools.native plugin only ever runs in the release job against the GraalVM that graalvm/setup-graalvm installs, and a plugin major that raises its minimum GraalVM has to land together with the action that provides it. Note the actual GraalVM version is selected by `java-version: '21'` in the workflow, which no manager covers today.
